html:
The Empire of Trebizond was a small Greek state on the Black Sea coast of north-eastern Anatolia, ruled from the port city of Trebizond (modern Trabzon) from 1204 to 1461. It was one of the pieces left when the Byzantine Empire broke apart.

It was founded in 1204, weeks before the crusaders sacked Constantinople. Its founders, Alexios and David, were grandsons of the emperor Andronikos I Komnenos, and they took the city with help from Queen Tamar of Georgia. Their family ruled for over 250 years as the "Grand Komnenoi".

The empire was tiny but well placed. Goods from Persia and Central Asia came overland through Tabriz to Trebizond and left by sea with Genoese and Venetian merchants. It survived by paying tribute to stronger neighbours, the Seljuks, then the Mongols of the Ilkhanate, and by marrying its famously beautiful princesses to Turkmen chiefs.

It outlasted Constantinople by eight years. In 1461 Mehmed II took it without a fight; see the fall of Trebizond.
sum: The Empire of Trebizond was a small Greek state on the Black Sea coast of north-eastern Anatolia, ruled from the port city of Trebizond (modern Trabzon) from 1204 to 1461. It was one of the pieces left when the Byzantine Empire broke apart.
